documentation.title: Design
documentation.value:
## Overview

This part encodes 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC) deaminase (AcdS: [BBa\_26MA70QI](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)) from *Pseudomonas putida* (Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus) strain UW4.

The part is a composite transcription unit with three elements, in this order:

* **Pveg (**Bba\_K143012**):** a constitutive bacterial promoter originally derived from *Bacillus subtilis* that drives continuous gene transcription without requiring external induction. 
* **EEBD-RBS0 (**[BBa\_26V6CPEV](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26v6cpev)**):** A composite ribosome binding site element containing a synthetic RBS sequence and expression-enhancing nucleotide context to improve translation initiation efficiency. EEBD is a blocking device, consisting of a B0015 terminator between two recombination sites to prevent unwanted gene expression or the production of toxic proteins while cloning DNA constructs inside *Escherichia coli*
* **SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag (**[BBa\_26NXOP7S](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26nxop7s)**):** a translational fusion of three elements:
  1. **SamyQ signal peptide (**[<u>BBa\_K1074014</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-k1074014)**):** N-terminal signal peptide of the *amyQ* gene, which encodes a highly efficient α-amylase natively found in *Bacillus subtilis* (and related lineages like *Bacillus amyloliquefaciens*). Csn and SamyQ were selected as candidates to determine which signal peptide offers higher secretion efficiency.
  2. **AcdS 2.1 (**[<u>**BBa\_262YYNPV**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-262yynpv)**):** the ACC deaminase coding sequence from [*Pseudomonas putida(Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus)*](https://www.uniprot.org/taxonomy/303) , with its native start codon and stop codon removed  In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence from AcdS wild-type ([<u>**BBa\_26MA70QI**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi)) were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site. 
  3. **6x Histag:** Fused at the C-terminus followed by a stop codon.This allows protein purification and identification after successful assembly and electroporation.
* **B0015** (BBa\_B0015): A high-efficiency double transcriptional terminator that stops RNA polymerase from continuing transcription past the CDS protectant, preventing transcriptional read-through into downstream modules.

The complete module was assembled by Golden gate assembly with BsaI-HFv2.

## About

* **Biosafety level:** S1
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* (168 / WB800)
* **Main purpose of use:** Constitutive expression and secretion of ACC deaminase
* **Potential application:** Lowering plant ethylene levels under stress, as a component of plant-growth-promoting bioprotectants.

## Literature

**Rationale.** ACC deaminase degrades ACC, the precursor of ethylene, and so can lower the ethylene levels that inhibit plant growth under stress (Hontzeas et al., 2004; Shah et al., 1998). The Csn signal peptide exports the enzyme from the cell, and the C-terminal 6x Histag allows detection and purification. The AcdS sequence comes from Q5PWZ8 (UniProt Consortium, n.d.; GenBank CP053102.1).

**Why a constitutive version.** We used the constitutive Pveg version in addition to the whole light-sensing construct because it lets us see the maximal secretion and protein production rate without the light switch. This version can be applied to plants and characterized directly by Western blot, which shows whether our constructs work under the most optimal conditions.

**Why Pveg and EEBD-RBS0.** Pveg gives high, continuous expression, so differences between protectants and signal peptides reflect the cargo rather than promoter strength. RBS0 sets translation initiation, and the EEBD protects *E. coli* during cloning. These are standard SubtiToolKit (STK) parts, so they assemble with the other protectant cassettes in the same format.

## Construction/assembly (wet lab)

* **Composite insert:** Pveg – EEBD-RBS0 – SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag – B0015, \[1848 bp]
* **Level 1 vector:** pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector (STK), \[ampicillin]
* **Template:** synthesized fragments assembled together
* **Annealing temperature (Level 0 amplification):** 60 °C
* **Assembly method (Level 1):** Golden Gate, \[BsaI-HFv2 enzyme]
* **Thermal cycle:**

| Temperature | Time   | Cycles    |
| ----------- | ------ | --------- |
| 37 °C       | 5 min  | 45 cycles |
| 16 °C       | 5 min  |           |
| 37 °C       | 10 min | 1 cycle   |
| 80 °C       | 20 min | 1 cycle   |

The full CDS was PCR-amplified as a single amplicon from the synthesized fragment using primers SamyQ F and ACCD R. Each primer carries a 5′ ATATAT spacer, a BpiI site (GAAGAC) for level 0 vector entry cloning, and a BsaI site (GGTCTC) for Level 1 assembly. The inner BsaI overhangs are TATG (incorporating the SamyQ start codon) at the 5′ end and TGTC at the 3′ end, which sets the CDS position and allows fusion to the downstream terminator. The amplicon was cloned into pSTK-0C-sfGFP and sequence-verified.

The Level 0 parts Pveg (BBa\_K143012), EEBD-RBS0 ([BBa\_26V6CPEV](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26v6cpev)), SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag ([BBa\_26TOGLX3](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26toglx3)) and B0015 (BBa\_B0015) were then combined in a single Golden Gate reaction (BsaI, T4 DNA ligase buffer, and T4 DNA ligase) into the pSTK-EXP1 expression shuttle vector, a Level 1 vector, in the order promoter, RBS, CDS, terminator. The reaction was transformed into *E. coli* DH5α, and positive clones were identified by colony PCR and sent for sequencing before electroporation into *B. subtilis*.

| Primer name    | Primer sequence (5′ to 3′)                         |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| pSTK-EXP-seq F | atagtcgatcggttcatcattcaccaaatca                    |
| SamyQ F        | ATATATGAAGACATCTGAGGTCTCATATGATTC AAAAACGAAAGCGGAC |
| ACCD R         | ATATATGAAGACATGAGGGGTCTCATGTCTTAATGATGATGATGATGAT  |
| pSTK-EXP-seq R | ctcactcattaggcaccccagg                             |

## Verification (wet lab)

Colonies from the pSTK-EXP1-sfGFP transformation were screened by colony PCR with backbone primers primers flanking the CDS insertion site, and the products were run on an agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder. A correct band runs at the expected size \[1984 bp]. Colonies producing a single, clean band at this size were considered positive candidates.

Positive candidates were then sequenced to confirm that the promoter, RBS, CDS and terminator are free of mutations and correctly ordered. Clones with a verified sequence were used for further experiments.

## Results

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/35ca22dd-7d68-44bb-a867-ca8762bbb236/bd64752e9f9845b52e51b9c289b7d91587aab8026c9931a3e3e67456f0444fc9.avif)

***Figure 1.*** **Colony PCR of pSTK-EXP1-Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag-B0015.** 1 of 1 colonies gave a band at the expected size (\[1984 bp]).

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/35ca22dd-7d68-44bb-a867-ca8762bbb236/9d5aa3d1fdfdfba9ecbbc349d2a6fabebe3df6f981daa89140e4f39ecae2cf1c.avif)

***Figure 2.*** **Clone 1 was sequence-verified and used downstream.**

documentation.title: Application
documentation.value:
This construct is the constitutive counterpart of the Light Responsive Expression Module in ccaSR-Csn-AcdS-Histag. It gives the maximal output of the same cassette, which the light-controlled version can be compared against. It was run in our bioreactor to monitor production and secretion, and its protein can be applied to plants for functional testing.

## Application-specific characterisation

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/5f1b23d8-f19d-4381-8291-cdf7ee694691/de3fe476b68b408de8943128c6b5fbe24ac2a45f0ead3a2e6a13ddec82a76f4c.avif)

**Figure 1.** *Arabidopsis thaliana* seedlings on vertical agar plates, photographed on day 15, after five days of thermo priming at 37 °C and five days of recovery at 22 °C. Top row, plates held at 22 °C throughout; bottom row, plates thermo-primed at 37 °C. Columns, left to right: no ACC deaminase added, pre-treatment, co-treatment, post-treatment. The protectant was a 0.22 µm-filtered culture supernatant from the Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-Csn-AcdS-B0015 construct in *Bacillus subtilis* secreting ACC deaminase, applied as three sprays totalling 0.536 mL above the root-tip line. Nine to ten seedlings per plate and one plate per condition, so the plate is the replicate. Three plates are marked "contaminated" on the panel itself: 22 °C co-treatment, 37 °C untreated and 37 °C co-treatment. Read off the panel: every 37 °C group is bleached and much smaller than its 22 °C counterpart, and within the heat-stressed row the pre- and post-treatment plates keep more yellow-green tissue than the near-white co-treatment plate. The panel carries colour and size only; it holds no measurement and no statistics, and the untreated heat-stressed plate it would be compared against is one of the contaminated ones.

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/5f1b23d8-f19d-4381-8291-cdf7ee694691/857f2439d39f13326110e56e38bf3eccad6954c2cb2692a2213975a6c229fa90.avif)

**Figure 2.** Quantitative readouts from the same agar thermo-priming set as PL01, scored on day 15. (a) Fresh weight in grams. (b) Relative chlorophyll a+b in mg g⁻¹ normalised to fresh weight. (c) Relative chlorophyll a+b in mg g⁻¹ without fresh-weight normalisation. (d) Primary root length in mm, as box plots over the individual seedlings. Each bar carries three points, shown as dots. Conditions are 22 °C or five days at 37 °C followed by five days of recovery, crossed with no ACC deaminase added, pre-, co- or post-treatment sprayed supernatant. The four-star brackets run from the untreated unstressed control to the other groups; they do not compare a treated group with its own untreated control inside the heat-stressed block. Read off the panel: among the 37 °C groups, pre-treatment ACC deaminase holds the highest chlorophyll in (c), about 0.09 against about 0.07 mg g⁻¹ for the untreated heat-stressed control, while co- and post-treatment fall to near zero; in (b) pre-treatment and the untreated heat-stressed control sit together at about 0.3, so the normalised readout separates them hardly at all. Fresh weight in (a) and root length in (d) separate the heat block from the 22 °C block but not the four application timings inside it. No panel here shows a statistically tested advantage of ACC deaminase over its untreated heat-stressed control, and that control plate was contaminated.

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/5f1b23d8-f19d-4381-8291-cdf7ee694691/4ff20787716175e2fc524b3544dacf848e7e73fad920c11e57f7759fe910951a.avif)

**Figure 3.** The hydroponic tube rack carrying the 37 °C heat run, photographed before the heat stress, with 15-day-old *Arabidopsis thaliana*. The rack carries both arms of that run: ACC deaminase at 1/40, 1/60, 1/80 and 1/100, BoPEP4 at the same four dilutions, and two controls repeated for each arm, 1/40 WB800 (the same TB medium carrying *Bacillus subtilis* WB800 with no protectant) and 0.1× MS medium alone. Three seedlings per labelled group, bracketed in red on the photograph. Read off the panel: at this point every group is a green rosette of broadly comparable size, which is the baseline the post-heat photograph is read against. The photograph is a before-state record and shows no treatment effect.

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/5f1b23d8-f19d-4381-8291-cdf7ee694691/426238dcca9822153edbd0c7448f38b36417cb11c9c53ec2a700cef63b54bf17.avif)

**Figure 4.** The same hydroponic tube rack as PL03, photographed after four days at 37 °C. Layout and labels are unchanged: ACC deaminase and BoPEP4 at 1/40, 1/60, 1/80 and 1/100, each arm with a 1/40 WB800 vehicle control and a 0.1× MS medium control, three seedlings per labelled group. Read off the panel: most rosettes on the rack have bleached to white or pale yellow, and the groups that retain visible green tissue sit in the ACC deaminase block and in the 1/40 BoPEP4 group. The photograph records colour and survival by eye; it is a single rack with no repeat, it carries no measurement, and the greener groups are identified by position on the rack, with no blinded score.

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/5f1b23d8-f19d-4381-8291-cdf7ee694691/bf0adfe3ac4613de62495985b768c385dd43ba645ec12b78c851adae3383bbf3.avif)

**Figure 5.** Readouts from the hydroponic 37 °C run shown in PL03 and PL04, 15-day-old *Arabidopsis thaliana* after four days at 37 °C. Three panels: fresh weight in g, chlorophyll content in µg per plant, and relative chlorophyll content as a ratio. Twelve groups per panel: ACC deaminase at 1/40, 1/60, 1/80 and 1/100, 1/40 WB800 (TB medium carrying *Bacillus subtilis* WB800 with no protectant) and 0.1× MS medium, each without heat and with heat. One bar per group, three seedlings per group pooled, with no error bars and no repeat of the run. Read off the panel: within the heat-stressed groups, all four ACC deaminase dilutions hold more chlorophyll per plant, about 2.6 to 3.1 µg, than the 1/40 WB800 vehicle control at about 2.1 µg and the medium-only control at about 1.7 µg; on relative chlorophyll, 1/40, 1/60 and 1/80 ACC deaminase sit at about 0.93 to 0.96 against 0.77 for the vehicle control and 0.86 for medium alone, while 1/100 is the lowest group at about 0.65. Fresh weight does not follow the same order: under heat the heaviest groups are 1/100 ACC deaminase at about 0.019 g and the 1/40 WB800 vehicle control at about 0.018 g, with 1/40, 1/60 and 1/80 ACC deaminase at about 0.014 to 0.015 g, below the vehicle control. The chlorophyll signal and the fresh-weight signal therefore disagree.

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/5f1b23d8-f19d-4381-8291-cdf7ee694691/f2d532ebc455d82512767ccd0cef4bd1ab080c5da6690643b7e5c4020d2dcc1f.avif)

**Figure 6.** The TB medium carrying *Bacillus subtilis* WB800 with no protectant, applied to *Arabidopsis thaliana* in the hydroponic rack at dilutions of 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 and 0 (no TB medium), at pH 5.7 and at pH 7.1. Three panels: fresh weight in g, chlorophyll content in µg per plant, and relative chlorophyll content as a ratio. Read off the panel: at both pH values fresh weight and chlorophyll rise monotonically as the TB medium is diluted out, and the groups receiving no TB medium at all are the highest on every readout, about 0.065 g at pH 5.7 and about 0.057 g at pH 7.1 against about 0.006 and 0.005 g undiluted. Even the mildest dilution tested here, 1/16, stays well below the no-TB group. The vehicle applied with every ReLEAF protectant is therefore not inert: it suppresses growth in a dose-dependent way, which is why the protectant runs were read against a matched 1/40 WB800 vehicle control rather than against medium alone.

documentation.value:
![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/05b4692d-e186-492b-af93-d2cca2ec8510/bd3754cc481d5ee3c211c055977a4ebff144f40a2f4253d5ded05ac314c9e726.avif)

**Fig. 1. Western blot analysis of constitutive ACC deaminase-2.1-Histag expression in *Bacillus subtilis*.** Detection was performed using a mouse monoclonal anti-Histag antibody. Immunodetection verified successful expression and secretion of ACC deaminase from the constitutive P<sub>veg</sub> promoter construct. Lane ACCD represents the culture supernatant in which a clear band was detected at approximately 37 kDa, consistent with the predicted size of the secreted ACCD.

documentation.title: Discussion
documentation.value:
**What the data mean.** ACCD is expressed in *B. subtilis* and secreted into the culture medium, so the construct works under optimal, constitutive conditions. Yield in the bioreactor was low, so there is room to improve it. Plant trials show the effectiveness of secreted protectants with our constructs.

**Limitations.** Western blots show presence and size, not enzymatic activity, and activity assays are still planned. Pveg, EEBD-RBS0, and B0015 are reused across modules, which creates a risk of homologous recombination in the full circuit.

**Future directions.** We plan to improve yield through promoter strength and codon optimization, measure ACC deaminase activity directly, and compare Csn with SamyQ.
